chapter_theme: Leaving the body (உடல்விடல்): the desires, speech, breath-sound, senses and mind that tie a person to the body fall away, and nothing, not even vows and gifts, is a sure support for the perishing flesh; the mind made firm stands before Siva.
structure_note: Two verses list what ends with the body (2139, 2140); the third sets the desire-driven wandering mind against the steadied mind before Siva (2141).

2139.reading: The desire that shapes a person, the speech one keeps up, the sound that shines in the breath, and the mind that clings to the sore-like body: when one looks upward, the body perishes.
2139.nuance: அண்ணாந்து பார்க்க carries the verse. Plainly it is the upturned gaze of the dying; in the yogic tradition it is taken as turning attention up to the crown, at which the body-bound faculties fall away. Both readings stand. பண்ணாக்கும் may mean 'that makes song' or 'that fashions'; புண்ணாம் உடல் calls the body a wound.

2140.reading: The ears of the perishing body, the vows and gifts of passing time, the speech that is spoken and the nadis that come to their end: none of these is a sure support for the flesh that is passing away.
2140.nuance: The participles அழிகின்ற, கழிகின்ற, மொழிகின்ற, முடிகின்ற, ஒழிகின்ற march the verse toward its end. The verse says vows and gifts do not hold up the body (ஊன்); it does not say whether they help the soul.

2141.reading: Desire rising at the leaf-slender waist and a mind sunk at the breast send one wandering, carrying a body brief as lightning; but the mind made firm as stone stands before Siva.
2141.nuance: மின்னுடல் may be the lightning-brief body or, in yogic reading, a body of light. சிலையாய சித்தம் may be a mind steady as stone or bent like a bow (சிலை is both), and சிவமுன் இடைக்கே is obscure, so the contrast drawn here is one reading.

links.note: The Kural calls virtue the companion that does not perish when one perishes; Tirumular says vows and gifts are no sure support for the perishing flesh. The two can agree if the Kural speaks of the person and Tirumular of the body; the verse does not settle which it means.
